 The 'Yellowstone' creator told Yahoo Finance he learned filmmaking on movie sets and won't compromise that standard
 By
 David Hookstead Fox News

 Taylor Sheridan has no apologies for spending big money on his television shows.
 Sheridan has become the king of entertainment and streaming after creating some of the most popular shows on TV .
 It all started with "Yellowstone," and only went up from there. His monster hits "Landman" and "Lioness" both came years afterwards and are also mega-hits. Tack on "Mayor of Kingstown," "Tulsa King" and other "Yellowstone" universe projects, and it's more than fair to say nobody comes close.
 TAYLOR SHERIDAN'S 'LANDMAN,' 'THE MADISON' SNUBBED BY EMMYS AS EXPERT HAILS HIM AS TV'S 'SIX-TIME CHAMPION' 
 Having said that, it definitely doesn't come at a cheap price. Sheridan previously said he believed the first season of "1923" was the most expensive first season of a show ever made. That's what happens with A-list casts and filming on massive locations in multiple states or countries.
 Taylor Sheridan defends massive budgets for his TV shows. ((Photo by CBS via Getty Images)) 
 Taylor Sheridan defends making shows with massive budgets.
 Sheridan recently spoke with Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi about several topics, and he was asked about the massive budgets his shows require.
 TAYLOR SHERIDAN'S $330M FOUR SIXES RANCH PURCHASE FORCED HIM OUT OF RETIREMENT PLANS 
 He didn't hesitate for a second that it's necessary and the only way to do it.
 Taylor Sheridan attends the black carpet during "Yellowstone" Season 5 Fort Worth Premiere at Hotel Drover on November 13, 2022 in Fort Worth, Texas. (Omar Vega/Getty Images) 
 "I mean they cost what they cost, right? And it's a constant battle, right, to sit there and they could argue, I'm sure that they would, that if we could have made Landman for $50 million less, they could have made $50 million more. But I disagree because now the product isn't as valuable and so you have less viewers. So it costs less, but you made less. So what are we trying to do? I'm a premium product maker. I only know how to do it one way. I learned how to direct and produce making movies. So, I only know how to do that. I don't know how to make a TV show, and I'm not trying to learn. I want them to look like movies," the "Yellowstone" creator explained.
 TAYLOR SHERIDAN TAKES SWIPE AT LOS ANGELES AFTER BUILDING TV EMPIRE FROM TEXAS 
 When asked how he handles high-level executives and money people at companies he works with, Sheridan dropped about as on-brand a line as you'll find.
 SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER 
 "Just don't call them back."
 Billy Bob Thornton as Tommy Norris in Landman episode 1, season 2, streaming on Paramount+. (Emerson Miller/Paramount+) 
 OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD 
 At the end of the day, you can't argue with Sheridan's methods . Again, he's responsible for the most successful shows on TV, and you can't have the casts and production value he routinely brings to the table without big budgets. The good news is the fans always respond, and it should be fun to see what Sheridan cooks up next. Let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com .
 David Hookstead is a reporter for OutKick.
